name: SDD - Spec-Driven Development
description: The fork's spec-driven build flow (Specify -> Clarify -> Planning -> Plan-Review -> Decompose -> Build (fan-out x6) -> Code-Review (join) -> Testing), expressed as a Pipeline graph on alamops/agetor#244's infrastructure. Wave 1 of docs/plans/sdd-pipeline-on-pipelines-infra.md -- token-efficiency re-hooking (lean context, CLAUDE.md filtering, deterministic handoff, precheck) is Wave 2, not yet wired in.

steps.name: Specify
steps.instructions: Write SPEC.md at the repository root: a clear, testable specification for the goal above — NOT the implementation. Do not name files, frameworks, or approach. Structure: ## Summary, ## User stories, ## Acceptance criteria (numbered "AC-N: <testable, behavioural criterion>" lines, sequential from 1, no gaps, no implementation details), ## Non-goals, ## Edge cases considered. Commit SPEC.md locally (do not push).

steps.name: Clarify
steps.instructions: Read SPEC.md. Scan it against this ambiguity taxonomy: functional scope, data shape, UX flow, non-functional requirements, integration behaviour, edge/failure handling, terminology. If you find material ambiguities and have ask_user available, ask (one at a time or grouped), then append a ## Clarifications section to SPEC.md recording each Q and answer, folded into the relevant AC inline. Otherwise append a ## Assumptions section recording how you resolved each one (lowest-risk conventional interpretation). Only append to SPEC.md, never rewrite existing content. Commit the update locally.

steps.name: Planning
steps.instructions: Read SPEC.md (authoritative for WHAT). Design HOW to build it: name the files/areas that change, the approach, and reference each AC-N by id rather than repeating its text. Do not restate requirements. Write PLAN.md at the repository root, concrete enough that a Builder can implement it from the file alone. Commit it locally.

steps.name: Plan-Review
steps.instructions: Read SPEC.md and PLAN.md. Check the plan against the actual codebase: does it address every AC-N at a design level, does it name real files/patterns, is the approach sound, would it break anything else? Do not write or change files. Write at most three bullet points, then a one-line verdict summary. This step is a human gate — end your turn without emitting a handoff `next` (leave it null and set status "blocked" with your verdict as the reason); a human reviews your notes in this step's own panel and manually advances to Decompose once satisfied, or sends you a follow-up with revision feedback.

steps.name: Decompose
steps.instructions: Read PLAN.md (approved) and SPEC.md. Decompose the plan into up to 6 independently-buildable slices — units of work implementable in isolation without seeing another slice's in-progress changes. If the plan doesn't decompose naturally, that's fine: use only slice 1. Count files touched first; fewer than 6 files or one component area = exactly one slice. Otherwise 2-4 slices sized by files touched, never one slice per file. No two slices may touch the same file/path — shared files (README, package.json, a global config) belong to exactly one slice, usually a final integration slice. There are 6 Build steps downstream (Build-1..Build-6); assign your real slices to Build-1, Build-2, ... in order and leave the rest unused. Write TASKS.json at the repository root: {"subtasks": [{"buildSlot": "Build-1", "title": "...", "prompt": "concrete self-contained instructions for exactly this slice", "acceptanceCriteria": ["AC-1"], "files": ["src/..."]}, ...]}. Commit SPEC.md/PLAN.md/TASKS.json locally (required — each Build step reads only what is committed here, not uncommitted working-tree edits). Your handoff's `artifacts` field must list the used buildSlot names (e.g. ["Build-1", "Build-2"]) so Code-Review's join knows which arrivals are real work vs no-ops.

steps.name: Build-1
steps.instructions: Read TASKS.json at the repository root. If it declares a subtask with buildSlot "Build-1", implement exactly that subtask per its prompt and PLAN.md (the acceptance criteria in SPEC.md are the testable definition of done). Commit your changes locally with a clear commit message (prefix the subject with "feature:"/"fix:" as appropriate; no AI attribution). If TASKS.json declares no subtask for buildSlot "Build-1" (or fewer real slices than 6 total Build steps), this is a no-op: do nothing, commit nothing, and end your turn immediately with a handoff reporting no work was assigned. Either way, do not push, do not open a pull request.

steps.name: Code-Review
steps.instructions: Read SPEC.md for the acceptance criteria and PLAN.md for the intended approach. Every arriving Build-N handoff in your prompt tells you which slices actually did work (a no-op slice's handoff says so — ignore those). Run `git diff` against the branch's base to see everything that's landed. Check: does the diff correctly implement PLAN.md, does it satisfy every AC-N at a code level, is the code quality sound (correctness, no obvious regressions)? Do not write or change files yourself, do not run the test suite or linters — Testing does that next. Keep context small: Read only relevant file ranges over 300 lines, pipe long shell output through `| tail -200`. Write at most three bullet points, then hand off to Testing (or, if something needs to change first, set status "blocked" naming what).

steps.name: Testing
steps.instructions: Run this project's linters, type-checker, and test suite. Read SPEC.md and verify every AC-N is actually exercised — by a test assertion or a manual check you perform yourself. If something fails and the fix is small and obviously correct, fix it directly; otherwise report it instead of guessing at a bigger change. Keep context small: pipe long output through `| tail -200`, Read only relevant file ranges over 300 lines. If you changed anything, commit locally with a clear message (no AI attribution, no push, no PR). End with a handoff summarizing pass/fail per AC; this is the last step in the graph (no outgoing edges), so the pipeline finishes here regardless of what `next` you set.
